items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The mention of 'Wes' occurs in the [INTERVIEWER]'s turn, comparing a guitarist's technique to Wes Montgomery's. The interviewee does not respond to this specific mention or discuss a personal relationship with Wes in the provided context.

ctx.x: "He doesn't have to be a virtuoso. I just want him to blend into the ambiance of what we're trying to do." Man, he hit it right on the money.
And with the thumb of Wes. And he was playing that way before he moved here, with his thumb like Wes does. We break for J.J. to take a phone call.
Another thing that I find very exciting about what’s happening in your life now and what’s been happening since you moved back to Indianapolis is your interest in teaching.
